q: can I give Motrin to my 8 month old for fever
text:
Yes, ibuprofen (Motrin) can be given to a child over 6 months old for fever, according to MedlinePlus [6]. Give it every 6 to 8 hours, and check the packaging or leaflet to be sure it suits your child [2][6]. Know your child's weight before giving it [6].

Do not give ibuprofen if your child is under 3 months, weighs under 5kg, has chickenpox, is dehydrated, or has asthma unless a doctor recommends it [1]. Do not alternate ibuprofen and paracetamol unless a doctor or nurse tells you to [1].

Keep giving plenty of fluids — if breastfed, continue as normal — and watch for signs of dehydration [2].

Get medical advice if:
- Your child is not their usual self or you are worried [1][2]
- Nappies are not very wet, eyes are sunken, or no tears when crying [1]
- The fever lasts 5 days or more [1]
- The medicine is not helping [2]

q: my son threw up twice this morning, what should I give him to drink
text:
Vomiting twice in a morning is often gastroenteritis, which is usually not serious in healthy people but can lead to dehydration, according to MedlinePlus [2]. The main thing is to keep fluids going in.

When he vomits, wait 20 minutes, then give oral rehydration solution — 2 to 5 ml every 5 minutes for an hour, says the SEUP [3]. Watch how he takes it: if he keeps it down, you can slowly give it more often [3]. Don't use homemade solutions like lemonade or commercial soft drinks [3]. Oral rehydration solutions for children can be bought without a prescription [5].

Get help if:
- He vomits a lot, can't keep down solids or liquids, or vomits even without drinking [7]
- Vomit is green, contains blood, or looks like coffee grounds [7]
- He is drowsy, limp, very thirsty, has sunken eyes, cries without tears, or urinates little [7]
- Severe belly pain or headache [7]
- Under 3 months old and has vomited two or more feeds [7]

q: how do I know if my child is getting dehydrated from vomiting
text:
Dehydration happens when the body loses more fluid than it takes in, and vomiting is one of the causes [1]. The main risk of vomiting is dehydration, according to the SEUP [3].

To prevent it, give oral rehydration solution: after a vomit, wait 20 minutes, then give 2–5 ml every 5 minutes for an hour [5]. If the liquids are tolerated, you can slowly increase how often you give them [5]. Do not use homemade solutions or commercial soft drinks [5].

Get help if your child:
- is very drowsy or floppy [3]
- vomits many times [3]
- will not take liquids [3]
- vomits even when not drinking, or vomits green, bloody or coffee-ground material [6]

If you think the dehydration is severe, call your doctor [2].

q: my 5 year old has been coughing all night, what can I do
text:
A cough that is worse at night is common with asthma and with viral colds in preschool children, according to the SEUP [1][3]. If your child has been diagnosed with asthma and has a reliever inhaler, give it now, using a spacer — never straight into the mouth, as it works less well that way [7]. If there is no clear improvement after the inhaler, take them to a health centre [7].

Get help if:
- They are very agitated or drowsy, or turn blue or pale [7]
- Breathing gets faster, ribs pull in, or the chest sucks in [7]
- Reliever inhalations are needed every two hours or less [7]
- They cannot speak properly or have continuous coughing [3]

Keep the home free of smoke, and avoid the things that trigger their symptoms [4][5].

q: my son has been coughing for a week after a cold
text:
A cough that lingers after a cold is common, and cold symptoms can last 10 to 14 days, according to MedlinePlus [6]. A cough lasting several weeks or months can also happen with whooping cough, which often starts like a cold and then brings coughing bouts, worse at night, sometimes with a "whoop" sound or vomiting after coughing [4].

What to do now: keep offering fluids, and avoid smoke or fumes, which can trigger coughing [1]. There is no home treatment in these sources that shortens a lingering cough.

Get help if:
- Your child has fits of rapid coughing followed by a "whoop" [3]
- Vomiting during or after coughing fits [3]
- Difficulty breathing after a coughing bout [4]
- Your child turns blue or grey [4]
- Your child is getting worse or not getting better [2]

If your child is under 3 months old and coughing like this, ask your doctor to see them [4].

q: he has a cough but no fever and is eating normally
text:
A cough without a fever, with normal eating, is usually caused by a common infection like a cough or cold, according to the NHS [1]. Keep offering fluids and let him rest; there is no need to treat a fever he does not have [5].

There is no specific home treatment for a cough without fever in the sources. If a fever does appear, the AEPap advises checking the temperature with a thermometer, and if there are no warning signs, starting with physical measures: removing extra clothing, giving fluids, reducing activity, and a lukewarm bath if he is comfortable [5].

Get help if:
- He is under 3 months and has a temperature of 38C (100.4 °F) or higher [1]
- He has a rash along with a high temperature [1]
- A high temperature lasts 5 days or more [1]
- He does not want to eat, or is not his usual self and you are worried [1]
- He shows signs of dehydration, such as nappies that are not very wet, sunken eyes, and no tears when crying [1]

q: my daughter has red spots all over her stomach and they appeared today
text:
Red spots that appear suddenly and itch can be hives, which in children are usually caused by an infection rather than an allergy, according to the SEUP [3]. The spots are raised, red patches that move around — fading in one area as they appear in another — and hives can usually be treated at home [3][5].

If they itch, a pharmacist can advise on antihistamine medicine, and a cool bath followed by patting the skin dry (not rubbing) can help, according to the NHS [1]. Dress your daughter in loose clothes and keep her fingernails short so scratching does not cause scarring [1]. Do not give ibuprofen unless a doctor tells you to, as it may cause serious skin infections [1].

Get help now if:
- swelling around the mouth [5]
- struggling to breathe [5]

Otherwise, see your doctor if the spots spread, blister, or she seems unwell.

q: my 2 year old has little red bumps on his legs and keeps scratching them
text:
It is common for a young child to get itchy red bumps, and hives is one cause, according to the NHS [1]. Hives look like raised, puffy bumps or patches that vary in size and can join together [1].

To ease the itching, a pharmacist can advise on antihistamine treatment for a hives rash [7]. Tell the pharmacist if your child has a long-term condition, and note this treatment may not be suitable for young children [7].

Get help straight away if:
- lips, mouth, throat or tongue suddenly swell [7]
- breathing is fast or struggling [7]
- throat feels tight or swallowing is hard [7]
- skin, tongue or lips turn blue, grey or pale [7]
- your child becomes very confused, drowsy or dizzy, or is limp and not responding [7]

These can be signs of a serious allergic reaction needing hospital treatment [7].

q: these spots dont seem to bother her but there are more every morning
text:
Spots that don't bother your child are often nappy rash, which is common in babies and can usually be treated at home, according to the NHS [2]. It can look like red or raw patches on the bottom or the whole nappy area, or spots, pimples or blisters that may be red or brown [2].

Keep the area clean and dry, change nappies often, and use a barrier cream at each change. If the spots are itchy, a pharmacist can advise on antihistamine treatment, though it may not be suitable for young children [7].

Get help if:
- The bottom becomes itchy or painful [2]
- Your baby seems uncomfortable or distressed [2]
- The skin becomes scaly and dry [2]
- Lips, mouth, throat or tongue suddenly swell [7]
- Breathing becomes fast or difficult [7]

q: my 6 year old fell from the bed and hit the back of his head
text:
Most head injuries in children are not serious, according to the NHS [2]. A bump on the back of the head can still cause concussion, a temporary brain injury that may last a few weeks [2].

What to do now: it is fine for him to sleep, but after a more significant knock it is worth waking him every 4 hours [6]. He can eat and drink as usual, according to his appetite [6]. If he has a headache, you can give paracetamol or ibuprofen at the dose your doctor indicates [6]. Keep him resting, away from sport and screens, for 24 to 48 hours [4].

Get help now if he:
- was knocked out or cannot stay awake [2]
- has a seizure [2]
- is vomiting repeatedly [4]
- is confused, or hard to wake [4]
- has clear fluid or blood from the nose or ears [4]

Watch him over the first 24 hours for a worsening headache, repeated vomiting, confusion, or trouble speaking or walking [3][4].

q: what foods should I start with for a baby who just turned 6 months
text:
Around 6 months, milk alone no longer meets all your baby's energy and nutrient needs, so solid foods are needed alongside it, according to the WHO [1]. Start with small amounts and increase them gradually as your baby grows, and build up the texture and variety of foods over time [1]. Offer 2–3 meals a day at this age, plus breast milk or first infant formula on demand — that's still where most of their energy and nutrients come from [1][2].

At the beginning, how much they eat matters less than getting used to eating [2]. Give one new food at a time so you can spot any allergic reaction, such as a rash, diarrhoea or vomiting, says MedlinePlus [5].

Do not give honey before their first birthday, and avoid cow's milk and unpasteurised foods and drinks before age one [5]. Whole nuts, popcorn, sweets and whole grapes are choking risks — cut grapes into small pieces [5].

q: how much water can a 9 month old drink
text:
For a 9-month-old, breast milk or formula remains the main drink, and water is not needed in large amounts. The WHO says to keep breastfeeding frequently, on demand, up to 2 years or beyond, and to increase fluids during illness, including more frequent breastfeeding [1]. The AEP says that between 6 and 12 months breast milk is still the main food and should be given on demand, without reducing the number of feeds [2]. If your baby is formula-fed, the AEP recommends a follow-on formula for babies over 6 months [2].

If you are giving water with meals, offer it in a cup in small amounts; the sources do not give a specific daily volume of water for this age. Do not add salt to your baby's food: babies need very little salt, and their kidneys are too immature to handle excess, so no salt should be added to complementary foods [2]. Up to 12 months, the maximum is less than 1 g of salt a day [3].

Ask your doctor how much water is right for your baby, especially if they are unwell.

q: my baby refuses vegetables but eats fruit all day
text: It is common for babies to prefer fruit, and the way to build vegetable acceptance is repeated, varied exposure rather than pressure. Offer the full range of fruits and vegetables across daily meals, changing how they are presented — puréed, mashed, in small pieces — and keep offering vegetables even when they are refused, because early exposure to different flavours, including bitter ones, makes them more likely to be eaten later, according to the AEP [2]. Include vegetables with bitter flavours such as broccoli, cauliflower, spinach and cabbage, alongside fruit, starchy foods, protein foods and full-fat dairy, as part of three meals a day plus milk feeds, according to the NHS [1]. Give whole fruit rather than fruit juice: juice offers no nutritional benefit over whole fruit, can displace other foods and increases the risk of tooth decay [2]. If your baby is under a year, avoid high-nitrate green leafy vegetables such as chard, spinach and borage, or keep them under 20% of the dish [2].

q: my daughter is 13 months and still mostly drinks formula
text:
At 13 months, formula alone is not enough — from 6 months on, children need complementary foods alongside milk, according to the WHO [1]. The first two years matter especially: good nutrition in this period lowers illness and supports growth and development [2].

What to do now: keep offering formula or breast milk, and add solid foods that are nutritionally adequate and safe, introduced from 6 months onward [1]. Offer a variety of foods and enough meals each day — worldwide, only about half of children 6–23 months get the number of meals they need [1]. Complementary feeding means giving these foods in addition to milk, not instead of it [5].

When to get help: ask your doctor or a feeding specialist if your daughter is not eating solids, is losing weight, or you are unsure how to move her on from formula — the AEP notes feeding advice should be part of health visits [3].

q: how often should a newborn poop
text:
How often a newborn poops varies from baby to baby — the rhythm and consistency of stools differ from one person to another, according to the SEUP [3]. What matters more than the number is the consistency: constipation is when stools become too hard, with discomfort or incomplete emptying, sometimes with fewer stools than usual [6].

For a baby under 6 months, keep feeding as usual with breast milk or formula [3]. Keep noting the baby's wet nappies and stools each day [5].

Get help if:
- Baby is very floppy or crying a lot [3]
- Blood in the stool [3]
- Vomiting many times, unable to keep down milk [3]

A baby this young who seems unwell should be checked by their doctor.

q: my 9 month old suddenly wakes up every two hours at night
text:
It is common and normal for a 9-month-old to wake at night: night wakings are physiological, and up to 20–40% of children under 3 wake during the night, according to the PUC Chile manual [2]. At this age a baby can sleep up to 5 hours at night, and each sleep cycle lasts about 90 minutes [2].

What helps is not to intervene each time, so a sleep habit does not form: the child should settle back to sleep on their own [2]. If a baby always falls asleep in your arms, on waking they will want the same conditions to fall asleep again [2].

Most infant insomnia is due to poor sleep habits and is a "family mental health" problem, not something that affects growth [6]. It does affect quality of life, causing irritability and poor attention [6].

If your baby seems unwell, or the waking comes with fever, feeding problems or unusual crying, see your doctor.

q: my 4 year old wakes up coughing only when he lies down
text:
A cough that comes on only when he lies down is one of the signs of asthma in children, according to MedlinePlus: coughing, especially at night or early in the morning, is a common symptom [5]. The SEUP also lists night-time cough among the symptoms of an asthma attack [3].

What to do now: keep a note of when the cough appears — at night, early morning, after running or playing, or after a cold — because that pattern is what your doctor will ask about [3][5]. There is nothing in these passages about a medicine to give at home for this.

Get help if:
- Severe coughing or serious trouble breathing [5]
- Face, lips or fingernails turning pale or blue [5]
- The cough is continuous or he has difficulty speaking [3]
- The chest pulls in and the ribs and collarbones show when he breathes [3]

These symptoms can be mild or severe and may come and go, so it is worth having him seen to find out what is causing the night-time cough [5].

q: my son has asthma and is using albuterol more than usual
text:
Using a reliever inhaler more often than usual can be a sign the asthma is not controlled, and it is worth having your son seen. Asthma cannot be cured, but inhalers control it and let children lead a normal, active life, according to the WHO [2].

Keep giving salbutamol with a spacer (and a mask for small children) — never straight into the mouth, because it works less well that way [3][7]. Most flare-ups are mild and can be treated at home with bronchodilators, and symptoms usually settle within a few days, though they can last up to a week [3]. Avoid smoke and, during the flare-up, exercise and allergens [3].

Get urgent help if:
- He is very agitated or drowsy, or turns blue or pale [7]
- Breathing gets worse: faster, ribs showing, belly or chest pulling in [7]
- He needs inhalers every two hours or less [7]
- No clear improvement after salbutamol [7]

If he has repeated flare-ups, he should carry his inhaler to school [3].

- Breathing difficulty appears [3]

q: she is making a strange noise when she breathes but is still smiling
text:
A strange noise when breathing can be stridor — a high-pitched sound — and it is one of the signs of croup, an inflammation of the voice box and windpipe that often starts like a cold, according to MedlinePlus [3]. Croup is most common between six months and three years, and symptoms usually get worse at night and last three to five days [3]. Most viral cases are mild and can be treated at home [3].

Keep her calm and comfortable, and let her rest; sitting her up can make breathing easier. Offer fluids often in small amounts.

Get help now if:
- Breathing becomes difficult or noisy at rest [3]
- The ribs pull in or the chest sinks with each breath [1][2]
- She seems drowsy, very irritable or floppy [1][4]
- Her colour looks bad [4]
- She cannot eat or drink [5]

If you are worried about her breathing, call your doctor right away [3].

q: my baby had a seizure last year and has a fever today
text:
A febrile seizure can happen when a child has a high temperature, and it is not usually serious, according to the NHS [3]. Most febrile seizures do not need treatment, but a child needs to be checked in hospital after a first febrile seizure [6].

If your baby has a seizure now: do not move them or hold them in place, do not put anything in their mouth, and do not try to lower their temperature by undressing them or sponging them with cold water [5].

Get help now if your child:
- has a seizure lasting more than 5 minutes [2]
- has trouble breathing [2]
- has stiffness and twitching on only one side [2]
- is more sleepy than usual for more than 1 hour after it stops [2]
- has more than one seizure within 24 hours [2]

You cannot prevent febrile seizures [6].

q: my 4 year old had a seizure when he was a baby, does that change anything now
text:
A seizure with a high temperature in a baby is called a febrile seizure, and it is unlikely to harm your child or cause long-term effects, according to the NHS [2]. They usually affect children between 6 months and 6 years old [5].

Having had one does not mean your child has epilepsy — they are not the same thing. Children who have had a febrile seizure have a slightly increased chance of having epilepsy later in life, but this is rare [3]. You cannot prevent febrile seizures [3].

If your child ever has another seizure:
- Check the time it starts and ends [4]
- Protect their head with your hands or something soft [4]
- Remove dangerous objects nearby [4]
- After it ends, put them in the recovery position [4]
- Do not put anything in their mouth or hold them still [1]

Get medical help if a seizure lasts more than 5 minutes, affects only one side, or they stay more sleepy than usual for over an hour afterwards [5].

A bee sting on the hand usually causes only pain, redness and swelling where the sting went in, according to MedlinePlus [2]. Most allergic reactions are mild, though a severe one called anaphylaxis can be serious [2].

100.4 °F = 38 °C.

- You are worried about your child [2]
- The medicine is not helping [2]

q: can babies get dehydrated from breastfeeding

q: should I give my daughter the HPV vaccine
text:
The HPV vaccine protects against human papillomavirus, a common virus spread through skin contact, usually during sex. Some types are linked to an increased risk of several cancers, including cervical, mouth, anal, penile, vulval and vaginal cancer, and genital warts, according to the NHS [1]. It works very well: since it has been used there has been a big drop in young people getting conditions linked to HPV, such as cervical cancer and genital warts [2].

In the United States, the ages and number of doses follow the national immunization schedule, so ask your doctor when your daughter is due [3].

Common side effects are mild and do not last long: pain or swelling where the injection was given, headache, a high temperature, dizziness, feeling sick, tiredness [5]. A severe allergic reaction is very rare, and the person who vaccinates is trained to treat it immediately [5].

q: my son missed his 4 month vaccines, what do we do now
text:
For a missed 4-month visit, the usual approach is to give the vaccines now rather than restart the schedule, according to the AEP [1]. Premature and at-risk babies should follow the same schedule as other babies, starting at 2 months of chronological age, regardless of gestational age or birth weight [1]. The dose is the same as for any other baby; there is no reason to use a reduced or split dose [1].

In the United States, the ages and doses follow the national schedule, so ask your doctor or clinic which vaccines your son needs now and when to bring him back.

Warning signs to get help:
- Fever, poor feeding, or unusual sleepiness after vaccination [1]
- Any sign that worries you [1]

q: my 11 year old needs a tetanus shot after a cut, does he need one
text:
No, an 11-year-old does not get DTaP — that vaccine is only for children younger than 7 years old, according to MedlinePlus [1]. Older children and adults receive different vaccines against tetanus, diphtheria, and pertussis, called Tdap and Td [1].

Whether he needs a tetanus shot after this cut depends on his vaccination history and the wound, which only his doctor can assess. Tetanus enters the body through cuts or wounds, and it is preventable with vaccines that contain tetanus toxoid [1][4].

Talk with your health care provider, and tell the vaccination provider if he has had an allergic reaction after a previous dose of any vaccine that protects against tetanus, diphtheria, or pertussis, or has any severe, life-threatening allergies [1].

q: my child has asthma but is not wheezing right now, should I still use albuterol
text:
No, if there is no wheezing or trouble breathing right now, the sources describe salbutamol as the treatment for an asthma attack — the episodes of cough, breathlessness and chest wheezing caused by narrowed airways — and not as something to give when the child is well [1][4]. The SEUP says that in any child having bronchospasm you start treatment with salbutamol, and that inhalers must always be given with a spacer, never straight into the mouth [7].

If an attack does start, give 2 to 4 puffs of salbutamol one at a time through a spacer, with a face mask for small children, and repeat that dose after 10 to 15 minutes [6]. Keep the child resting, away from tobacco smoke and pollution, and continue any maintenance treatment during the attack [6].

Get help if:
- Very agitated or drowsy, or turning blue or pale [7]
- Breathing gets faster, ribs pull in, belly moves a lot [7]
- Puffs needed every two hours or less [7]
- No clear improvement after treatment at home [6]

text:
If your child is under 3 months old, a fever needs a doctor the same day.

Cold hands and feet with a fever happen because the body narrows the blood vessels in the skin to raise its temperature, according to the SEUP [7]. This is part of how fever works, and it does not mean the fever itself is dangerous [5].

What to do now: check the temperature with a thermometer, under the arm is fine [5]. If there are no warning signs, start with physical measures — take off extra clothing, offer plenty of fluids, reduce activity, and a lukewarm bath only if the child is comfortable [5]. Do not undress or sponge the child to cool them, and do not wrap them in too many clothes or blankets [2]. If the child is uncomfortable with a fever above 38°C (100.4 °F), give the antipyretic your paediatrician usually recommends [6]; the dose depends on age and weight.

Get help if:
- Drowsy, not reacting, or very irritable [1]
- Trouble breathing [1]
- Spots that do not fade when pressed [1]
- Will not take solids or liquids [1]
- Under 2 months old or immune-compromised [1]

text:
Confusion after a knock to the head is one of the symptoms the SEUP lists for head injury, and it is a reason to seek emergency care [1][3].

While you get help, keep him still and do not let him go back to sleep unattended; the SEUP says to watch a child closely in the first 24 hours after a blow to the head for signs of seriousness [2]. Do not give him anything to eat or drink in case he needs tests.

Get emergency care now if he has any of these, according to MedlinePlus:
- Confusion that is getting worse, or restlessness [4]
- Repeated vomiting or nausea [4]
- A headache that gets worse or does not go away [4]
- Trouble speaking, or weakness or numbness in the arms or legs [4]
- Fits, or trouble waking up [4]

The SEUP also says to go to the emergency department if the fall was from more than one metre, or if the child is under three months old [3].

What to do now: get plenty of rest and drink lots of fluids [5]. If your child is uncomfortable, you can give paracetamol or ibuprofen — check the leaflet if you are not sure it is suitable [5]. - Coughing fits make it hard to breathe [2]
- Your child is exhausted after coughing fits [3]
- The cough lasts several weeks or months [4]

q: my 2 year old weighs 40 pounds, should I be worried
text:
40 lb = 18.1 kg.

A 2-year-old boy at 40 pounds is above the average for his age, but weight alone does not tell you whether it is a problem — it has to be looked at together with his height [1]. From age 2, your child's weight and height can be used to work out their body mass index (BMI) and plot it on a growth chart, which is how you check whether their weight is in the healthy range [1]. The World Health Organization says that for children under 5, being overweight is a weight-for-height more than two standard deviations above the median, and obesity is more than three [6]. Ask your pediatrician to measure his height and plot his BMI on the growth chart at his next visit; if he is above the healthy range, they can give you advice about his diet and activity levels [1].

Note: 18.1 kg is very high for a child of 2 years on the WHO growth charts. If it was a typo, correct it, because doses go by weight; if it is right, mention it to your doctor.

q: my son had croup last winter and now has a barking cough again
text:
A barking cough that comes on suddenly at night, after a few days of cold-like symptoms, is the usual picture of croup, according to the SEUP [3]. It is most often mild and can be treated at home [1].

Keep your son calm and comfortable — crying or getting upset makes the noise worse, because faster breathing makes it seem louder [3]. Offer fluids if he has a fever, and give his usual fever medicine [4]. Water can help ease the cough, whether he drinks it or you add it to the air with a steamy shower or vaporizer [6].

Get help if:
- His breathing becomes difficult [1][2]
- He makes a high-pitched, rasping sound when breathing in [2]
- His colour or general condition changes [4]
- He is getting worse or not getting better [2]

Most children improve within a few days, though it can last up to a week [4].

q: what should I know about malaria symptoms in a child returning from Africa
text:
Malaria is a potentially deadly infection spread by mosquito bites, and children under 5 are at higher risk of severe illness, according to the WHO [1]. Early symptoms are often mild and easy to mistake for other fevers: fever, headache and chills, usually appearing 10 to 15 days after an infected bite [2]. Because the symptoms are not specific, get a test as soon as possible [2]. Early treatment of a mild case can stop it getting worse [5].

Severe signs — get emergency care quickly:
- Extreme tiredness or fatigue [2]
- Confusion or reduced awareness [2]
- Seizures [2]
- Difficulty breathing [2]
- Dark or bloody urine, yellow eyes or skin, unusual bleeding [2]

Untreated falciparum malaria, the most common type in Africa, can become severe and cause death within 24 hours [2].

After resting, children usually recover quickly, within a couple of minutes [5]. She can sit up first, then stand after a few minutes [5]. Encourage her to drink more fluids, especially with exercise [4].

Get help if:
- Unconscious for more than 3-5 minutes [6]
- Fainted during exercise or effort, or while sitting [6]
- Palpitations, chest pain, jerking limbs, or wetting herself [6]

A temperature of 105 °C is not possible in a living child — that reading is almost certainly a mistake or a different unit. Fever is a body temperature above normal, usually around 37 °C (98.6 °F), and it is not an illness itself: it is a sign the body is fighting an infection, according to MedlinePlus [1]. Most fevers in children are caused by infections, and they are usually harmless and self-limiting [6].

Check the thermometer and take the temperature again, in the armpit, with a digital thermometer [6]. If the child is not showing warning signs, start with physical measures: remove extra clothing, offer fluids, reduce activity, and give a lukewarm bath only if the child is comfortable [6]. Antitérmicos are only for discomfort, not to bring the temperature to normal [6].

Get help if:
- The child is drowsy, confused or hard to wake [5]
- A seizure happens [5]
- The child cannot be calmed, or cries uncontrollably [5]
- The child is dehydrated or breathing with difficulty [5]

In an asthma attack, the airways narrow and this improves with a bronchodilator such as salbutamol, according to the WHO [1]. The SEUP says that in any child with bronchospasm you should start treatment with salbutamol [4].

Use the inhaler with a spacer, and a mask for small children — never straight into the mouth, because it works less well that way [4]. Most attacks are mild and can be treated at home with bronchodilators; symptoms usually settle within a few days, though they can last up to a week [3]. Avoid smoke and keep them away from allergens, and skip exercise during the attack [3].

Get help if:
- Very agitated or drowsy, or turning blue or pale [4]
- Breathing gets worse: faster, ribs or chest pulling in [4]
- Needing inhalations every two hours or less [4]
- No clear improvement after salbutamol [4]

q: my 9 month old still has no teeth, is that normal
text:
It is normal for a 9-month-old not to have teeth yet. The first tooth usually shows between 4 and 8 months of age, according to MedlinePlus [4].

Until then, wipe your baby's gums with a damp washcloth after each meal [4]. Do not put them to bed with a bottle of milk, juice or sugar water — use only water for bedtime bottles [4]. Once the first tooth appears, switch to a soft toothbrush [4].

Ask your child's health care provider whether your baby needs oral fluoride [4]. Take your child to a dentist every 6 months, and let the dentist know if they suck their thumb or breathe through the mouth [1].

q: my child has chickenpox, when can he go back to school
text:
Children usually miss 5 to 6 days of school or childcare because of chickenpox, according to the CDC [1]. A child with chickenpox can pass it on until all the spots have crusted over, so they should stay home until then [2].

While they are home: keep them comfortable, and calamine cream or lotion and oatmeal baths can help with the itching [3]. Paracetamol can help with fever [3]. Do not give aspirin — with chickenpox it can cause Reye's syndrome [3].

Chickenpox is usually mild and lasts 5 to 10 days [3], though the illness itself usually lasts about 4 to 7 days [1].

Get medical help if:
- The rash looks infected or spreads widely [3]
- They have trouble breathing [3]
- They seem very drowsy or confused [3]
- They are not drinking or are dehydrated [3]

Some children — babies, teenagers, pregnant women and those with weakened immune systems — can get more serious illness and may need antiviral medicine [3].

q: she bumped her forehead on the table and cried right away, do I need to watch her
text:
A bump on the head is usually minor, because the skull is hard and protects the brain, according to MedlinePlus [3]. The SEUP says most head injuries in children are mild and not dangerous [4].

For the next 24 hours, keep an eye on her for any of the signs below [4]. Let her rest, and keep her away from sports and screens for 24 to 48 hours [2]. She can eat normally, and she can sleep — if the knock was a hard one, it is worth waking her every 4 hours [5]. If she has a headache, paracetamol or ibuprofen at the dose your doctor gives is fine [5].

Get help if she has:
- A headache that gets worse or does not ease [3]
- Repeated vomiting [2]
- Confusion, or being hard to wake [2]
- Trouble speaking or walking [2]
- Blood or clear fluid from the nose or ears [2]

Also go if she is under three months old, or fell from more than a metre [7].

q: I read that vaccines can cause autism, is that actually true
text:
No, that is not true: many scientific studies have looked at this and found no link between vaccines and autism, according to MedlinePlus [1]. Vaccines are safe, and they must go through extensive safety testing and evaluation before they are approved in the United States [1].

If you are wondering when your child should get their vaccines, they are given at well-child visits, following the vaccination schedule [4]. In the United States, the CDC publishes that schedule, which lists the recommended vaccines, how many doses are needed and at what age they should be given [4]. Following it lets your child build immunity before being exposed to very serious diseases [4].

q: my daughter has a seizure right now, what do I do
banner: 🚨 Call 911 now or go to the emergency department. | Reason: Abnormal movements / seizure
text: Lay your child on their side in a safe place, away from anything they could hit, and put nothing in their mouth, according to the SEUP [6]. Stay with them and, if you can, note the movements and how long the seizure lasts [6]. Time it: febrile seizures usually last 2 to 3 minutes, and it is rare for them to last more than 10 minutes, according to the NHS [2]. Protect their head with your hands or something soft and move dangerous objects away [5]. Once the seizure ends, put them in the recovery position and check nothing is blocking their mouth or throat [5]. If they have not had fever medicine in the last 2 hours, you can give paracetamol or ibuprofen [6]. After a febrile seizure, they should be checked by a doctor [6].

q: is the MMR vaccine safe for my baby I read online it causes autism
text:
The MMR vaccine is safe, and there is no evidence it causes autism. Studies have found no link between the MMR vaccine and autism, according to the NHS [1]. Many scientific studies have looked at this and found no link between vaccines and autism, according to MedlinePlus [5].

Children need 2 doses of MMR vaccine, usually the first at age 12 through 15 months and the second at age 4 through 6 years, following the United States schedule [6]. It can be given at the same time as other vaccines [6].

Serious allergic reactions are rare and usually happen within minutes, and the person who gives the vaccine is trained to treat them right away [7].

Talk to your child's doctor if you are worried about your child having a vaccine or are not sure whether they can have it [7].

q: my baby has yellow skin, is that normal at 3 days old
banner: 🚨 With these symptoms your child should be seen in the emergency department today, without waiting. | Reason: Baby with yellow skin or eyes: urgent appointment today. If under 24 hours old, very sleepy, not feeding, feverish or no wet nappies, go to emergency now
text:
Jaundice at around 3 days old is common in newborns and is usually harmless, getting better without treatment, according to the NHS [1]. For most babies with jaundice, the yellow is most noticeable when they're around 3 days old, and it usually takes around 2 weeks to go [1].

Because your baby is under 3 months old, they need to be assessed by a doctor today. While you arrange that, keep feeding them as usual and watch their nappies.

- is sleepier than normal or difficult to wake [1]
- is not feeding [1]
- is floppy or stiff, or has jerking or twitching movements [1]
- has a temperature of 38C (100.4 °F) or more, or 36C (96.8 °F) or less, or feels hot or cold [1]
- has dark yellow or brown pee, or pale creamy poo [1]

q: she has a fever and cold hands and feet, is that normal
banner: 🚨 With these symptoms your child should be seen in the emergency department today, without waiting. | Reason: Cold hands and feet in a child with fever: it may be poor circulation, get it checked
text:
If your child is under 3 months old, a fever needs a doctor the same day. For an older child, a fever is the body's normal response to fighting an infection, such as a cough, cold, chickenpox or tonsillitis, according to the NHS [2].

Cold hands and feet in a child with a fever can be a sign of poor circulation, and the NHS lists unusually cold hands and feet as a reason to get emergency help [2]. While you get help, do not undress your child or sponge them down to cool them, and do not cover them in too many clothes or bedclothes [2].

Get help now if your child:
- has a stiff neck [2]
- has a rash that does not fade when you press a glass against it [2]
- is bothered by light [2]
- is drowsy and hard to wake, or is confused [2]
- has difficulty breathing, or skin, lips or tongue that look blue, grey or paler than usual [2]

q: my baby is making fewer wet diapers today
banner: 🚨 With these symptoms your child should be seen in the emergency department today, without waiting. | Reason: Signs of dehydration: sunken eyes, little urine, dry mouth, persistent vomiting or heavy diarrhoea >24 h
text:
Fewer wet diapers than usual is a sign of dehydration in a baby, according to the NHS [4]. In infants and young children, dehydration symptoms include no wet diapers for 3 hours or more, a dry mouth and tongue, crying without tears, and eyes that look sunken [6].

Keep offering fluids. If your baby is breastfed, keep breastfeeding normally and even more often if they want it [1]. If they are having diarrhoea, oral rehydration solution is what replaces the losses — not homemade solutions or commercial soft drinks [7]. Give small amounts often, and let their appetite guide you [1].

Get medical help right away if there is also confusion, fainting, lack of urination, rapid heartbeat or rapid breathing [6]. Also seek care if your baby is very irritable, unusually sleepy or hard to wake, is refusing to drink, or cannot drink as fast as they are losing fluid [7].

q: my daughter has hives after eating eggs but no trouble breathing
text:
Hives are raised, itchy red patches that move around — appearing in one area as they fade from another — and most hives in childhood are caused by an infection, with allergic causes being less common, according to the SEUP [1]. They can come with swelling of the hands, feet, elbows or face, and only exceptionally with trouble breathing or swallowing [1].

If your daughter has hives but is breathing normally, the SEUP says the main thing to watch for is exactly that: difficulty breathing or swallowing, which is exceptional but needs urgent help [1].

Get help if:
- Trouble breathing or swallowing [1]
- Swelling of the face, hands, feet or elbows that worries you [1]

For the itching itself, ask your doctor or pharmacist what antihistamine is right for her age and weight.

q: she feels hot but the thermometer says 98.6
text:
A temperature of 98.6°F is normal, not a fever — a normal temperature is generally around 98.6°F or 37°C (98.6 °F), according to MedlinePlus [4]. A fever means a temperature above 38°C (100.4°F) [5]. If she feels hot but the thermometer reads normal, she may just have been wrapped up or recently bathed; wait a few minutes and take it again [1].

If she does turn out to have a fever, the goal is her comfort, not bringing the number down [2]. Keep her well hydrated, in a comfortably cool, ventilated room, and don't over-bundle her [2]. It's normal for her to have less appetite — don't force her to eat, but offer plenty of fluids [2]. Paracetamol or ibuprofen can ease her discomfort; the right amount depends on her weight, so follow what your doctor recommends [2].

Get medical help if she:
- has a rash along with the fever [7]
- has a fever lasting 5 days or more [7]
- is not eating or not herself, and you're worried [7]
- seems dehydrated — fewer wet nappies, sunken eyes, no tears [7]
- has a stiff neck, is hard to wake, or is breathing with difficulty [7]

q: my child may have swallowed a magnet
banner: 🚨 With these symptoms your child should be seen in the emergency department today, without waiting. | Reason: Swallowed an object or something is stuck in the throat (batteries, magnets, a fish bone)
text:
A single swallowed magnet often passes without problems, but swallowing more than one magnet can cause serious bowel problems, according to the SEUP [6]. Do not try to make your child vomit, and do not give water, milk, oil or any other food [3]. If you can see something solid in the mouth and can reach it, take it out — never blindly [3]. - has strong, continuous belly pain that gets worse [5]
- is vomiting, or vomits green, brown or bloody material [4]
- has black, tar-like stools or blood in the stool [4]
- has a tense, hard or swollen belly [4]
- has fever [6]

While you travel, keep your child away from any remaining magnets and watch their breathing and colour [3].

q: my child has a rash after having a fever, could it be from the fever
text:
If your child is under 3 months old, a fever needs a doctor the same day.

For an older child, a rash that appears just as the fever drops is a recognised pattern. According to the SEUP, fever usually lasts two to four days [1]. A common cause in babies and toddlers is roseola: three to four days of high fever with no other symptoms, then the fever falls and a faint, flat, widespread rash appears that is not itchy and lasts about 48 hours [2]. The diagnosis is made from this sequence of events [2].

There is no specific treatment for the rash itself. If the fever is making your child uncomfortable, paracetamol is the first choice and ibuprofen is an alternative; the dose depends on your child's age and weight [5].

q: what are the side effects of chickenpox shot
text:
Most side effects of the chickenpox vaccine are mild and do not last long, according to the NHS [1]. They can include swelling or pain where the injection was given, a high temperature, and a rash at the injection site or more widespread, usually developing within 1 month of vaccination [1].

Serious side effects, such as a severe allergic reaction, are very rare, and the person who gives the vaccine is trained to treat allergic reactions immediately [1].

Get help if:
- Swelling or pain at the injection site that worries you [1]
- A high temperature [1]
- A rash appearing within a month of the shot [1]
- Any sign of a severe allergic reaction [1]

The chickenpox vaccine is given on the United States national schedule; ask your doctor about the ages and doses for your child.
sources: [1] NHS — "Chickenpox vaccine" (2024), section "Side effects of the chickenpox vaccine", p

q: my baby has a cough and sounds very congested when sleeping
text:
For a cough and a blocked, noisy nose, the usual cause is a common cold, and it is not dangerous in itself. There is no medicine that cures it, so the aim is to keep your baby comfortable and breathing easily.

Offer feeds little and often, and keep your baby upright against your shoulder for a while after feeding. Saline drops in the nose, then gentle suction with a bulb syringe, can clear the congestion before feeds and sleep. Keep the room free of smoke, and let your baby sleep on their back in their own cot, free of toys, blankets and pillows, as this lowers the risk of sudden infant death syndrome, according to the NHS [3].

Get help if:
- your baby is struggling for breath [7]
- your baby stops breathing or will not wake up [7]

An ear infection is the most common reason parents bring a child to the doctor, and pulling at the ear with crying more than usual is one of the signs to look for, according to MedlinePlus [1]. Most ear infections get better on their own within 3 days, according to the NHS [3].

For the pain, MedlinePlus says your health care provider may recommend pain relievers [1]. The SEUP advises treating the pain regularly for the first 1 to 2 days, before it builds up, and not putting anything in the ear to soothe it [6]. Keep the ear dry, especially if it has been discharging, and if your baby is a infant, do frequent nasal washes with saline [6]. - High temperature [3]
- Discharge from the ear [3]

q: my toddler has very hard poop and cries when he goes
text:
Hard, painful poops are constipation: the stool is hard and dry and it can hurt to pass [3]. It is common and in most cases it lasts a short time and is not serious [3].

What helps, according to the SEUP: offer more liquids, preferably water, to soften the stool and make it easier to pass; add more fibre — wholegrain cereals and bread, fruit, vegetables; and do not replace fruit with juice, because juice has little fibre [1]. Keep to a regular routine and don't hold back the urge to go [1]. Laxatives or enemas should not be given without asking your paediatrician [1]. It is not essential that a child poops every day — the rhythm and consistency vary from person to person [1].

See a doctor if, according to the SEUP:
- Severe abdominal pain, or a child who is very down and complaining a lot [1]
- Blood in the stool [1]
- Vomiting many times, unable to keep down solids or liquids [1]
- Pain when passing stool, or anal fissures [2][4]

Some babies sleep much more than others, and every baby has their own pattern of waking and sleeping [1]. Growth spurts, teething and illnesses can all affect how a baby sleeps [2].

If your baby wakes up and feeds normally, keep feeding on demand and let them sleep as they need. Try to rest when your baby sleeps [1].

A cough that is worse at night is common in several childhood illnesses, and the cause is not always clear from the cough alone. In croup, a barking cough that sounds like a seal, a hoarse voice and noisy breathing are often worse at night, according to the NHS [3]. Whooping cough causes coughing bouts that are worse at night and may end in a "whoop" or vomiting [4].

- Your child is struggling to breathe or breathing noisily [3]
- The cough is getting worse or not improving [3]

q: my child keeps scratching red patches on his arms
text:
Itchy red patches on the arms are most often eczema, which is not contagious and is common in babies and children [2]. It causes dry, itchy skin and scratching can make it redder and itchier [2].

What helps: keep the skin moisturised and avoid things that irritate it, such as certain soaps, fabrics and lotions, and stress [2]. Treatment can include medicines, skin creams and light therapy, so see your doctor about what suits your child [2].

See your doctor if:
- The itching is severe or the skin is broken, weeping or crusted [2]
- It is not getting better with skin care [2]
- Your child also has a rash spreading over the body [2]

If the patches are very itchy at night, with small bumps or lines on the fingers, wrists or arms, it may be scabies, which needs a doctor's diagnosis and treatment [3][6].

q: my 3 year old is coughing mostly at night, should I use a nebulizer
text:
A night-time cough in a 3-year-old can have several causes, and asthma is one of them: coughing that is worse at night or early in the morning is a common symptom, according to MedlinePlus [4]. The NHS says asthma symptoms may also be worse at night and early in the morning [6].

A nebulizer is not something to start on your own. If your child has asthma symptoms, the NHS advises seeing a doctor, and also if symptoms are waking them up at night or treatments are not helping [6].

Get help if:
- Severe coughing or serious breathing problems [4]
- Turning very pale or blue in the face, lips or fingernails [4]
- Difficulty breathing after a coughing bout [2]
- A barking cough like a seal, or a rasping sound when breathing in [3]

Coughing itself helps clear the airways, and water — drunk or as steam — can ease it, according to MedlinePlus [5]. Children under four should not have cough medicine [5].

q: my son has been vomiting since morning and cannot keep ORS down
banner: 🚨 With these symptoms your child should be seen in the emergency department today, without waiting. | Reason: Vomits everything and keeps nothing down: it is a danger sign — get seen today
text:
A child who keeps vomiting and cannot keep fluids down needs to be seen today, and the most important risk of vomiting is dehydration, according to the SEUP [6]. While you get help, keep offering small sips of oral rehydration solution often, and continue breastfeeding or formula in small amounts more often than usual [7]. Do not give fruit juice or fizzy drinks, and do not water down formula [7].

Get help now if:
- Vomiting is green, contains blood, or looks like coffee grounds [4][5]
- The child is drowsy, floppy, very thirsty, has sunken eyes, cries without tears, or is passing little urine [4]
- Severe tummy pain or headache [4]
- Vomiting everything, tolerating no solids or fluids, or vomiting even without drinking [4][5]

q: मेरे बच्चे को कल से दस्त हो रहे हैं और वह खाना नहीं खा रहा
banner: 💛 यह ज़रूरी है और आप अकेले नहीं हैं। Tele-MANAS 14416 पर कॉल करें (या 112 पर अगर खतरा अभी है)। अगर बच्चे ने खुद को नुकसान पहुँचाया है, तो अभी इमरजेंसी ले जाएँ। | कारण: खानपान के विकार के संकेत
text:
दस्त आमतौर पर किसी संक्रमण का लक्षण है और यह कुछ दिनों तक रह सकता है, जिससे शरीर में पानी और नमक की कमी हो सकती है [4]। WHO के अनुसार दस्त का इलाज ओरल रिहाइड्रेशन सॉल्यूशन (ORS) से किया जाता है, और इसके साथ ज़िंक की पूरक खुराक भी दी जाती है, जो दस्त की अवधि और मात्रा दोनों को कम करती है [2][4]।

अभी यह करें: ORS का घोल पिलाएँ — यह साफ़ पानी, नमक और चीनी का मिश्रण है [2]। खाना बंद न करें; बच्चे को पौष्टिक भोजन — ज़रूरत पड़ने पर स्तनपान भी — दस्त के दौरान जारी रखें, थोड़ी-थोड़ी मात्रा में और बार-बार, बच्चे की भूख का सम्मान करते हुए [2][6]। चिकनी चीज़ें, मिठाइयाँ और जूस से बचें; स्पोर्ट्स ड्रिंक न दें [6]।

मदद कब लें:
- मल में खून [2][3]
- बार-बार बहुत पतले दस्त या बार-बार उल्टी [3]
- बहुत ज़्यादा प्यास लगना [3]
- कुछ भी न पी पाना या स्तनपान न करना [3]
- बेसुध होना, जागने में कठिनाई, तेज़ साँस [3]

q: मेरे बच्चे को बुखार के साथ लाल दाने निकल आए हैं
text:
अगर बच्चा 3 महीने से छोटा है, तो बुखार में उसी दिन डॉक्टर को दिखाना ज़रूरी है।

बुखार के साथ लाल दाने कई बीमारियों में हो सकते हैं। खसरे में दाने पहले लक्षणों के 3 से 5 दिन बाद निकलते हैं — आमतौर पर बालों की लाइन पर चेहरे से शुरू होकर गर्दन, धड़, हाथ-पैरों तक फैलते हैं, और दाने निकलते समय बुखार तेज़ हो सकता है, CDC के अनुसार [4]। चेचक में खुजली वाले दाने शरीर पर कहीं भी हो सकते हैं, और दानों से पहले या बाद में तेज़ बुखार, दर्द और भूख न लगना भी हो सकता है, NHS के अनुसार [5]। हाथ-पैर-मुँह रोग में पहले गले में दर्द, तेज़ बुखार और खाने का मन न करना, फिर मुँह के छाले और हाथ-पैरों पर उभरे दाने होते हैं [3]।

इनमें से कौन-सी बीमारी है, यह डॉक्टर ही बता सकते हैं। दाने दिखने पर डॉक्टर को दिखाएँ।

मदद तुरंत लें अगर:
- बच्चे के मुँह के आसपास सूजन हो या साँस लेने में तकलीफ़ हो [6]

बच्चे की उम्र कितनी है? उम्र जानकर मैं जवाब और सटीक कर सकता हूँ।

q: मेरा 6 महीने का बच्चा दूध कम पी रहा है और पेशाब भी कम कर रहा है
banner: 🚨 इन लक्षणों के साथ बच्चे को आज ही इमरजेंसी में दिखाना चाहिए, देर न करें। | कारण: पानी की कमी के लक्षण: आँखें धँसी, कम पेशाब, सूखा मुँह, लगातार उल्टी या 24 घंटे से ज़्यादा दस्त
text:
नमस्ते। आपके बच्चे की स्थिति को लेकर आपकी चिंता बिल्कुल जायज़ है। चूँकि ऊपर चेतावनी संकेत दिखाए गए हैं, कृपया बच्चे को तुरंत डॉक्टर के पास ले जाएँ।

रास्ते में, SEUP के अनुसार, बच्चे को स्तनपान सामान्य रूप से और ज़रूरत पड़ने पर और भी अधिक बार कराते रहें [1]। अगर बच्चा माँ का दूध नहीं पी रहा, तो ओरल रिहाइड्रेशन सॉल्यूशन (ORS) छोटी-छोटी मात्रा में बार-बार दें [1]। बच्चे को भूखा न रखें; अगर वह खा सकता है तो सामान्य आहार थोड़ी-थोड़ी मात्रा में और अधिक बार दें [1]। चिकित्सक के निर्देश मिलने तक कोई भी दवा अपने मन से न दें।

डॉक्टर से मिलते समय ये बातें ज़रूर बताएँ:
- बच्चा बहुत उल्टी कर रहा हो या कुछ भी निगल न पा रहा हो [1]
- उल्टी हरी हो, उसमें खून हो या कॉफ़ी जैसे भूरे कण हों [1]
- पेशाब बहुत कम हो रहा हो या बिल्कुल बंद हो गया हो [3]

कृपया देर न करें — बच्चे को तुरंत चिकित्सकीय सहायता दिलाएँ।
sources: [1] SEUP — "Gastroenteritis aguda. Información para padres" (2025), section "¿DEBEMOS OFRE
[3] NHS — "Urinary tract infections (UTIs)" (2025), section "Urinary tract infections (UTI

q: मेरी बेटी बिस्तर से गिर गई और उसके बाद एक बार उल्टी हुई
banner: 🚨 इन लक्षणों के साथ बच्चे को आज ही इमरजेंसी में दिखाना चाहिए, देर न करें। | कारण: सिर पर चोट के बाद उल्टी
text:
सिर की चोट के बाद उल्टी होना एक ऐसा लक्षण है जिस पर तुरंत डॉक्टर से जाँच करानी चाहिए, और SEUP के अनुसार अस्पताल की आपातकालीन सेवा में जाना चाहिए यदि बच्चा तीन महीने से छोटा हो या गिरावट एक मीटर से अधिक ऊँचाई से हुई हो [1]। डॉक्टर आवश्यक जाँच करेंगे और तय करेंगे कि अतिरिक्त परीक्षण चाहिए या नहीं, हालाँकि ज़्यादातर मामलों में इसकी ज़रूरत नहीं पड़ती [1]।

रास्ते में बच्चे को आराम से रखें और उनका ध्यान रखें। अगर उल्टी हो रही हो तो बार-बार थोड़ा-थोड़ा पानी या तरल दें, और शिशु को स्तनपान या बोतल से दूध पिलाते रहें — अगर उल्टी हो रही हो तो थोड़ी-थोड़ी मात्रा में बार-बार दूध दें [5]।

अगर बच्चा बेहोश हो, सुस्त हो, ठीक से जवाब न दे, या साँस लेने में तकलीफ हो, तो तुरंत आपातकालीन मदद लें [4]।

q: बच्चे को कब्ज है और पॉटी करते समय बहुत रोता है
text:
नवजात या छोटे बच्चों में कब्ज के कारण पॉटी करते समय तकलीफ़ और रोना हो सकता है, और कब्ज उन कारणों में से एक है जिनसे बच्चा रोता है, ऐसा NHS कहता है [2]।

अगर बच्चा लगातार रो रहा है और आप उसे चुप नहीं करा पा रहे हैं, या रोना उसके सामान्य रोने जैसा नहीं लग रहा, तो यह बीमार होने का संकेत हो सकता है — ऐसे में अपने डॉक्टर से संपर्क करें [4]।

मदद लें अगर:
- बुखार हो या दूध/खाना लेना बंद कर दे [4]
- रोने के बीच बच्चा सामान्य न हो, पीला पड़ जाए, पसीना आए या सुस्त लगे [6]
- उल्टी हो या पॉटी में खून आए [6]
- पिछले 8 घंटे में पेशाब की नैपी गीली न हो [4]
- त्वचा, होंठ या जीभ नीली, स्लेटी या पीली दिखे, या बच्चा जाग न रहा हो [4]

अगर आपको समझ न आए कि क्या गड़बड़ है, तो अपने डॉक्टर से बात करना सबसे अच्छा है [2]।

q: मेरे बच्चे के हाथ पैर ठंडे हैं लेकिन शरीर गर्म है
text:
बुखार के दौरान हाथ-पैर ठंडे होना आम बात है: जब बुखार चढ़ रहा होता है तो बच्चे को ठंड लगती है, कभी-कभी कंपकंपी भी होती है, और खासकर हाथों-पैरों की त्वचा पर जाल जैसा धब्बेदार रंग दिख सकता है। जब बुखार उतरता है तो बच्चा पसीना-पसीना हो जाता है, लाल पड़ जाता है और उसे गर्मी लगती है, ऐसा SEUP बताता है [2]।

बुखार का मतलब है शरीर का तापमान 38°C से ऊपर, और यह शरीर के अपने बचाव का संकेत है — ज़्यादातर मामलों में इसकी वजह साधारण, अक्सर वायरल, संक्रमण होता है [4]।

अभी के लिए: बच्चे को ढेर सारे तरल पदार्थ देना ज़रूरी है ताकि पानी की कमी न हो [1]। बुखार से परेशानी हो तो डॉक्टर पैरासिटामोल या आइबुप्रोफेन जैसी दवा की सलाह दे सकते हैं; बच्चों को एस्पिरिन नहीं देनी चाहिए [1]। दवा की मात्रा बच्चे के वज़न पर निर्भर करती है।

डॉक्टर से मिलें अगर: बच्चा बहुत सुस्त या बेचैन लगे, कमज़ोर महसूस करे, या पेशाब कम आए [1]।

q: मेरा बच्चा बहुत सुस्त है और ठीक से जाग नहीं रहा
banner: 🚨 अभी 112 पर कॉल करें या तुरंत इमरजेंसी ले जाएँ। | कारण: जवाब नहीं दे रहा; बहुत ज़्यादा सुस्ती या चिड़चिड़ापन
text:
बच्चे का सुस्त होना और ठीक से जाग न पाना गंभीरता का संकेत है, और ऐसे लक्षण दिखते ही तुरंत अस्पताल ले जाना चाहिए [2]। विकासपीडिया के अनुसार निमोनिया में बच्चा सुस्त हो जाता है और ज़्यादा देर जागता नहीं है, और ये खतरे के लक्षण हैं [2]।

जब तक मदद मिले, बच्चे को अपने पास रखें और उसका खान-पान चालू रखने की कोशिश करें [2]। अगर बुखार है, तो गुनगुने पानी में कपड़ा भिगोकर पूरा शरीर पोंछें, सिर्फ माथा नहीं [2]।

अस्पताल पहुँचने पर डॉक्टर बताएँगे कि कौन-सी दवा और कितनी मात्रा में देनी है [2]।

q: मेरे बच्चे ने आज बहुत कम पेशाब किया है

text:
बच्चे का पेशाब कम आना अक्सर इस बात का संकेत होता है कि वह पर्याप्त तरल नहीं पी रहा; एनएचएस के अनुसार पेशाब का गाढ़ा रंग या तेज़ गंध अकेले इसी कारण हो सकता है कि पर्याप्त पानी नहीं पिया गया [3]।

अब जो करें: बच्चे को बार-बार थोड़ी-थोड़ी मात्रा में तरल दें, खासकर पानी, ताकि वह दिन में नियमित रूप से पेशाब करे और प्यासा न लगे [4]। अगर दस्त या उल्टी भी है, तो एसईयूपी के अनुसार खाना बंद करने की ज़रूरत नहीं — सामान्य आहार थोड़ी-थोड़ी और बार-बार दें, चिकनी चीज़ें, मिठाई और जूस से बचें, दूध और स्तनपान जारी रखें, और स्पोर्ट्स ड्रिंक न दें [1]।

मदद कब लें:
- उल्टी बहुत हो या तरल भी न रुके [1]
- उल्टी हरी, खून वाली या कॉफ़ी जैसी भूरी हो [1]
- पेशाब में जलन या दर्द, बुखार, पीठ या पेट के निचले हिस्से में दर्द [3]

q: मेरी बेटी को तेज बुखार और बैंगनी जैसे दाग हो गए हैं

text:
अगर बच्चा 3 महीने से छोटा है, तो बुखार में उसे उसी दिन डॉक्टर को दिखाना ज़रूरी है [2]।

बड़े बच्चे में तेज़ बुखार आम बात है और आमतौर पर 1 से 4 दिनों में तापमान सामान्य हो जाता है, ऐसा NHS कहता है [3]। त्वचा पर बैंगनी या ऐसे दाग जो दबाने पर नहीं मिटते, गंभीर संक्रमण का संकेत हैं — SEUP के मुताबिक ऐसे दाग होने पर तुरंत अस्पताल ले जाना चाहिए [1]।

अभी यह करें: बच्चे को ज़्यादा कपड़ों या रज़ाई में न लपेटें और ठंडा करने के लिए कपड़े उतारकर स्पंज न करें — तेज़ तापमान शरीर की स्वाभाविक प्रतिक्रिया है [2]। बच्चे को पानी या तरल थोड़ा-थोड़ा करके पिलाते रहें [1]। 16 साल से कम उम्र में एस्पिरिन न दें [2]।

- बच्चा सुस्त, कम प्रतिक्रिया वाला या बहुत चिड़चिड़ा हो [1]

- कुछ भी खाना-पीना न ले पाए [1]

q: mere 3 saal ke bacche ko bukhar 102 hai, paracetamol kitna du
text:
3 saal ke bacche ko bukhar 102 hai, to paracetamol bukhar aur bechaini mein aaram deta hai, NHS ke mutabiq [1]. AEPap kehti hai ki antitérmico tab dein jab bukhar 38-38.5°C se zyada ho ya bachche ko takleef ho [3].

Paracetamol har 4-6 ghante mein diya ja sakta hai, din mein paanch se zyada baar nahi [3]. Dawa ki matra bachche ke wazan se tay hoti hai, umar se nahi [3]. PediBot ka dose calculator paracetamol ke liye maujood hai [3].

AEPap ke mutabiq, agar bachche ko koi khatre ka ishara nahi hai to pehle kapde kam karein, taraL dein, activity ghataayein aur gungune paani se nahiLaayein [6]. Sote hue bachche ko dawa dene ke liye jagayein nahi [6].

Madad lein agar:
- Bukhar 3-4 ghante baad bhi zyada hai aur takleef kam nahi hoti [3]
- Bachcha sust ya bechain lage [3]
- Dawa se pehle hi ulti ho jaye [5]

q: mera baby raat ko bahut khans raha hai
text:
Aapke baby ki raat ki khansi ke baare mein: SEUP ke mutabik sardi-zukam (catarro) mein khansi aam hai, aur bachche saal mein 6 se 8 baar zukam se grasit ho sakte hain [4]. Agar khansi ke saath saans phoolna, seene ka dhadakna ya seeti jaisi awaaz ho, to yeh asthma ke lakshan ho sakte hain [5].

Ghar par: bahut saara taraल द्रव (paani, doodh) pilayein aur aaram karayein [2]. Saaf humidifier ya thande bhaap wala vaporizer istemal karein, aur saline nasal drops ya spray dein [3]. Khansi ya zukam ki dawa dene se pehle apne doctor ya pharmacist se poochein — bachchon ke liye kuch ingredients theek nahi hote [3]. Aspirin bilkul na dein [3].

Turant madad lein agar:
- Saans lene mein takleef ya tez saans [3]
- Hothon ke aas-paas neela rang [5]
- Bukhar 4 din se zyada [3]
- Lakshan 10 din se zyada bina sudhaar [3]
- Paani ki kami (dehydration) [3]

Agar aapke baby 1 saal se chhota hai aur khansi ke daure bahut tez hain, to doctor se turant milein [1].

q: mere bete ke pairon par lal dane hain aur khujli ho rahi hai
text:
Chhote, ubhre hue lal dane jo khujli karte hain, aksar heat rash (prickly heat) hote hain — yeh takleef deta hai par aam taur par harmless hai aur kuch dinon mein khud theek ho jata hai [6].

Ghar par sabse zaroori hai skin ko thanda rakhna taaki pasina aakar rash ko na chidhaye: dheele cotton kapde pehnao, halka bistar use karo, thande paani se nahao, aur paani zyada pilao [6]. Khujli ya chubhan ke liye thandi cheez — geele kapde ya ice pack (toliya lapet kar) — 20 minute tak lagao, aur rash ko kuraidne ke bajaye thap-thap karo [6]. Perfume wale shower gel ya cream mat lagao [6].

Turant madad lein agar:
- Munh ke aas-paas sujan ho [5]
- Saans lene mein dikkat ho [5]

text:

q: mere bacche ko kabz hai aur potty karte waqt rota hai
text:
Bacche ka kabz aur potty karte waqt rona: SEUP ke mutabik kabz un wajahon mein se ek hai jiski wajah se chhote bacche bahut rote hain, aur yeh kabhi kabhi lactant cólico se juda hota hai [2]. Agar bacche ko kabz hai, to pehle yeh dekhein ki woh potty karte waqt dard ya takleef mehsoos kar raha hai ya nahi.

SEUP ke anusar, cólico ke dauran bacche apni mutthi band karte hain, chehra laal ho jata hai, ghutne pet ki taraf uthate hain ya kamar mod lete hain, aur pet mein gudgudi ya gas hoti hai [3]. Kabz mein bhi aise hi lakshan dikh sakte hain.

Ghar par kya karein: SEUP ke mutabik, cólico mein aksar aap sirf bacche ko tasalli de sakte hain aur rone ke khatam hone ka intezaar kar sakte hain [1]. Kabz ke liye, bacche ko hydrate rakhein aur pet par halki malish karein.

Madad kab lein: Agar bacche ko kabz ke saath yeh lakshan hon to apne doctor se milein — 8 ghante se zyada peshab na aana, bahut zyada ulti, ya sust ya behosh hona [7].

text:
Mere bachche ko saans lene mein dikkat ho rahi hai — yeh ek aisi sthiti hai jismein turant madad lena zaroori hai. SEUP ke mutabik, saans lene mein dikkat (pasliyan dikhna, seene ka dhasna, tez saans, chalne ya daudne mein thakan) ek aisa lakshan hai jise dekhkar turant emergency seva mein jaana chahiye [7].

Jab tak madad pahunchti hai, bachche ko seedha aur aaram se rakhein, aur unhe kuch bhi khilane-pilane ki koshish na karein. NHS ke anusar, agar bachcha saans lene mein dikkat kar raha ho — ghurghurahat, pasliyan andar khinchana, ya tez saans — to yeh gambhir sthiti hai [5].

RSV ya bronchiolitis jaisi sthiti mein shuruaat mein zukaam jaise halke lakshan hote hain, lekin kuch dino mein saans lene mein dikkat badh sakti hai [2][4]. Isliye der na karein.

Turant medical madad lein.

q: meri beti bahut sust hai aur jag nahi rahi

text:
Aapki beti ki susti aur jag na paana gambhir lakshan ho sakte hain. WHO ke mutabik, bachchon mein sepsis ke lakshan hain: tez saans, jhatke, pale skin, susti, aur jag nahi paana [2]. SEUP ke mutabik, agar bachcha bahut sust ho ya jagane mein dikkat ho, to turant aspatal le jaana chahiye [3].

Jab tak madad aa rahi hai, bachche ko karwat par litaa kar rakhein aur uske munh mein kuch na daalein [3]. Uske saans lene aur chehre ke rang par dhyan dein [2].

Agar bachche ko tez bukhar, thandi aur pasine wali skin, ya peshab kam aa raha ho, to ye bhi gambhir lakshan hain [2].

text:
तेज़ साँस लेना शिशुओं और छोटे बच्चों में ब्रोंकियोलाइटिस या RSV जैसी साँस की बीमारी का लक्षण हो सकता है, जिसमें साँस तेज़ चलती है और बच्चा ठीक से दूध या खाना नहीं ले पाता [3][4]।

अभी बच्चे को गोद में सीधा रखें और शांत रखें, और थोड़ी-थोड़ी मात्रा में बार-बार दूध या तरल दें ताकि वह पानी की कमी से न घबराए [3]। अगर नाक बंद है तो उसे साफ़ रखें ताकि साँस लेने और दूध पीने में आसानी हो [3]।

डॉक्टर से तुरंत मिलें अगर:
- साँस लेते समय पसलियाँ अंदर धँसती दिखें या घरघराहट हो [3]
- साँस लेने में रुकावट या लंबे विराम पड़ें [3]
- होंठ, जीभ या चेहरा नीला या स्लेटी दिखे [3]
- बच्चा बहुत सुस्त हो और जगाने पर भी न जागे [3]
- 12 घंटे से ज़्यादा पेशाब न आए या बहुत कम दूध पिए [3]

अगर आपको लगे कि बच्चा गंभीर रूप से बीमार है, तो अपनी परख पर भरोसा करें और तुरंत मदद लें [3]।

q: my 2 year old has bad cough at night not sleeping
text:
A cough that is worse at night and stops a 2-year-old sleeping can be whooping cough, according to the NHS: after about a week it causes coughing bouts that last for a few minutes and are worse at night [2]. The cough may last several weeks or months [2].

Keep the room cool and give small sips of water often. The coughing fits get worse and happen more often, especially at night, and can last up to 10 weeks or more, according to MedlinePlus [3].

Get help now if:
- Lips, tongue, face or skin turn blue or grey [4]
- Hard or shallow breathing [4]
- Chest pain worse when breathing or coughing [4]
- Seizures (fits) [4]
- A very bad cough that is getting worse [4]

If your child has a barking, seal-like cough with a hoarse voice or a rasping sound when breathing in, that may be croup, which is also often worse at night [5].

q: my 5 year old baby has red pimples on full body
text:
A rash that spreads over the whole body can be measles, which the WHO describes as starting with high fever, cough, runny nose and red, watery eyes, followed by a rash that begins on the face and neck and moves down over about three days to the torso, arms, legs and feet [1][4]. The rash usually lasts four to eight days and then fades on its own [4].

There is no treatment for measles itself, but the MMR vaccine prevents it, according to MedlinePlus [2]. Keep your child comfortable and give plenty to drink.

Get medical help if you notice:
- Trouble breathing or pneumonia signs [4]
- Severe diarrhoea or dehydration [4]
- Ear infection signs [4]
- Confusion, drowsiness or seizures [4]
- Eye problems or blindness [4]

Measles can be more serious in children under five, so it is worth having your child checked [4].

q: my 6 year old child is not eating anything from 2 days
text:
It is common for children to refuse food for a while, and it is more helpful to think about what they eat over a week rather than in a day, according to the NHS [5]. If your child is active, gaining weight and seems well, they are likely getting enough to eat [5].

Keep offering a variety of foods and try again another time; children's tastes change and it may take many attempts before they accept a food [5]. Give small portions and praise them for eating, even a little, and do not force them to eat [2]. Do not leave meals until they are too hungry or tired, and keep snacks to about two a day between meals [2].

Get help if:
- Much thirst, crying without tears, little urine, sunken eyes [1]
- Marked irritability, drowsiness or reduced responsiveness [1]
- Refusing to eat or drink [1]
- Persistent or intense tummy pain, or stools with a lot of blood [1]
- Vomiting a lot, not keeping down solids or liquids, or vomit that is green, bloody or like coffee grounds [3]

q: my 6 month old baby has congested chest and making whistling noise
banner: 🚨 With these symptoms your child should be seen in the emergency department today, without waiting. | Reason: Breathing difficulty: fast breathing, wheezing, ribs pulling in
text:
A whistling or wheezing noise with a congested chest in a 6-month-old is often caused by a viral respiratory infection, and in preschool children viral infections are the main cause of wheezing, according to the SEUP [4]. Bronchiolitis often starts like an ordinary cold with cough and mucus, and after 2 to 4 days breathing can become harder — breathing faster, irritability, and difficulty feeding [6].

Keep feeding them: small, frequent feeds, and watch that they are drinking and having wet nappies. Keep their nose clear of mucus so they can feed and sleep.

Get help now if:
- Breathing fast or ribs pulling in [3][6]
- Grunting noises when breathing [2]
- Struggling to breathe, choking or gasping [2]
- Pale, blue or blotchy skin, lips or tongue [2]
- Too tired to feed or drink, or hard to wake [3][2]

Wheezing is more common with viral infections, according to the WHO [3].

q: bukhar (उम्र: 6 महीने) (वज़न: 5 किलो)
text:
बुखार छोटे बच्चों में बहुत आम है और आमतौर पर 1 से 4 दिनों में अपने आप उतर जाता है [1]। 38°C या उससे ज़्यादा तापमान बुखार माना जाता है [1]।

अभी यह करें: बच्चे को खूब तरल दें — अगर स्तनपान कराती हैं तो सामान्य रूप से स्तनपान जारी रखें [3]। जितना चाहे उतना खाना दें [3]। रात में भी नियमित रूप से बच्चे को देखती रहें [3]। बच्चे को घर पर ही रखें [3]। अगर बच्चा बेचैन या असहज लगे तो पैरासिटामोल या आइबुप्रोफेन दें — पैकेट या पर्ची देखकर पक्का करें कि दवा आपके बच्चे के लिए ठीक है [3]। 6 महीने के बच्चे को आइबुप्रोफेन न दें अगर वज़न 5 किलो से कम हो, चिकनपॉक्स हो या दस्त से पानी की कमी हो [2]। एस्पिरिन 16 साल से कम उम्र के बच्चों को न दें [2]।

डॉक्टर से मदद लें अगर: बच्चा खाना नहीं चाहता या अपनी सामान्य अवस्था में नहीं लगता और आपको चिंता हो [2]; बुखार 5 दिन या ज़्यादा रहे [2]; पेशाब कम आना, धँसी आँखें, रोते समय आँसू न आना जैसे पानी की कमी के संकेत हों [2]; बुखार के साथ दाने हों [2]।

ध्यान दें: WHO के विकास चार्ट के अनुसार 6 महीने के बच्चे के लिए 5 किग्रा बहुत कम वज़न है। अगर वज़न सही है तो जल्द ही डॉक्टर से बच्चे की बढ़त जँचवाएँ; अगर लिखने में गलती हुई है तो उसे ठीक करें, क्योंकि दवा की खुराक वज़न से तय होती है।

q: क्या बुखार उतारने के लिए बच्चे को नहला सकती हूँ? (उम्र: 6 महीने) (वज़न: 5 किलो)
text:
बुखार में बच्चे को नहलाना या स्पंज करके ठंडा करने की कोशिश न करें — यह शरीर की स्वाभाविक और स्वस्थ प्रतिक्रिया है, ऐसा NHS कहता है [7]। बच्चे को ज़्यादा कपड़ों या रज़ाई में न लपेटें [7]।

बुखार उतारने के लिए गुनगुने पानी में कपड़ा भिगोकर पूरा शरीर पोंछें, सिर्फ माथा नहीं, और बच्चे का खाना-पीना चालू रखें, ऐसा भारत स्वास्थ्य कहता है [3]। पैरासिटामॉल बुखार के लिए दी जा सकती है [3]।

डॉक्टर से मिलें अगर:
- 3 से 6 महीने का बच्चा और तापमान 39C या ज़्यादा [7]
- बुखार के साथ दाने [7]
- बुखार 5 दिन या ज़्यादा रहे [7]
- बच्चा खाने-पीने को राजी न हो, स्तनपान भी न करे [3]
- बच्चा सुस्त हो जाए, ज़्यादा देर जागे नहीं [3]

साँस लेते समय पसलियाँ अंदर खिंचें, कराहट या सीटी जैसी आवाज़ आए, या त्वचा, होंठ, नाखून पर नीली झलक दिखे तो तुरंत वैद्यकीय सहायता लें [3]।

ध्यान दें: WHO के विकास चार्ट के अनुसार 6 महीने के बच्चे के लिए 5 किग्रा बहुत कम वज़न है। अगर वज़न सही है तो जल्द ही डॉक्टर से बच्चे की बढ़त जँचवाएँ; अगर लिखने में गलती हुई है तो उसे ठीक करें, क्योंकि दवा की खुराक वज़न से तय होती है।

q: 3 साल के बच्चे को सूखी खांसी और छाती से सीटी की आवाज आ रही है
banner: 🚨 इन लक्षणों के साथ बच्चे को आज ही इमरजेंसी में दिखाना चाहिए, देर न करें। | कारण: साँस की दिक्कत: तेज़ साँस, सीटी जैसी आवाज़, पसलियाँ दिखना
text:
सूखी खांसी और सांस लेते समय सीटी जैसी आवाज़ ब्रोंकियल ट्यूबों में रुकावट से होती है, जिसे "सिबिलेंस" कहते हैं, और यह अक्सर सांस की वायरल बीमारियों के कारण होती है, SEUP के अनुसार [2]। ऐसे में बच्चे को सीधा बैठाकर रखें और शांत रखें, और सांस लेने में तकलीफ हो तो तुरंत मदद लें [2]।

डॉक्टर से मिलें अगर:
- खांसी भौंकने जैसी लगे या आवाज़ बैठ जाए [3]
- सांस लेने में तकलीफ या तेज़ सांस [3]
- बच्चा दूध या खाना न ले रहा हो [3]
- होंठ या चेहरा नीला पड़ जाए [7]

q: मेरे 5 साल के बच्चे के शरीर पर लाल दाने हो गए हैं और खुजली है
text:
लाल दाने और खुजली कई कारणों से हो सकते हैं। बहुत खुजली वाले उभरे हुए दाने छोटे कीड़ों (स्केबीज़) से हो सकते हैं, जो त्वचा में घुसकर अंडे देते हैं; उंगलियों के बीच एक सिरे पर बिंदु वाली उभरी लकीरें दिख सकती हैं, और स्केबीज़ का इलाज आमतौर पर घर पर ही हो जाता है [4]। स्केबीज़ में तेज़ खुजली और दाने होते हैं और यह त्वचा के सीधे संपर्क से फैलता है [2]।

घर पर: ठंडे पानी से नहाएँ और त्वचा को थपथपाकर सुखाएँ, रगड़ें नहीं; ढीले कपड़े पहनाएँ; खुजली के लिए फार्मासिस्ट से एंटीहिस्टामिन के बारे में पूछें [5]। नाखून छोटे काटें और रात में हाथों में मोज़े पहनाएँ ताकि बच्चा खुजाए नहीं [5]। खुजली शुरू होने के बाद कुछ हफ़्तों तक बनी रह सकती है [1]।

मदद लें अगर:
- त्वचा में संक्रमण लगने का संदेह हो [1]
- एक्ज़िमा जैसी कोई और त्वचा समस्या हो [1]
- कोहनी, घुटनों, हाथों या पैरों पर पपड़ीदार परतदार दाने हों [1]
- फार्मेसी का इलाज पूरा होने के 2 से 4 हफ़्ते बाद भी खुजली बनी रहे [1]

स्केबीज़ का इलाज क्रीम या मुँह से ली जाने वाली दवाओं से होता है [2]।

q: क्या एमएमआर वैक्सीन बच्चे के लिए सुरक्षित है
text:
एमएमआर वैक्सीन सुरक्षित है — सभी टीके काफी सुरक्षित हैं, और होने वाले दुष्प्रभाव मामूली से लेकर गंभीर तक हो सकते हैं, पर इनका मामूली उपचार से इलाज हो जाता है [6]। दुष्प्रभाव होना इस बात का संकेत है कि वैक्सीन असर दिखा रही है [6]।

भारत में टीके राष्ट्रीय टीकाकरण कार्यक्रम के तहत लगाए जाते हैं, और उम्र तथा खुराक भारत के राष्ट्रीय शेड्यूल के अनुसार तय होती हैं [2]। टीका लगवाने से पहले कोल्ड चेन का ध्यान रखा गया हो और एक्सपायरी तिथि बाकी हो, यह जाँच लें [2]। कोई भी वैक्सीन शत-प्रतिशत प्रभावशाली नहीं होती [2]।

अपने बच्चे के टीकों की उम्र और अगली खुराक के बारे में अपने डॉक्टर या स्वास्थ्य कर्मी से पूछें [3]।

q: 3 saal ke bacche ko raat ko bahut khansi aati hai
text:
Raat ki khansi asthma ka ek aam lakshan hai — bachchon mein khansi khaas taur par raat ko ya subah jaldi hoti hai, aur kabhi-kabhi yeh sirf khansi se shuru hota hai [5][7]. SEUP ke mutabiq, agar saans phoolne ki dikkat ho to salbutamol se ilaaj shuru kiya jata hai, aur inhaler hamesha spacer (chamber) ke saath dena chahiye, seedha muh mein nahi [7].

Ghar par: kamre ki hawa saaf rakhein, dhuan aur tambaku ke dhuen se bachayein, kyunki fumo karne wale maa-baap ke bachchon mein saans ki bimariyan zyada hoti hain [7]. Bahut saara paani pilayein aur aaram karne dein [4]. Khansi ya dard ke liye koi bhi dawa dene se pehle apne doctor ya pharmacist se poochhein — bachchon ko aspirin bilkul nahi deni chahiye [4].

Turant madad lein agar:
- Bahut bechain ya sust/neend mein [7]
- Hont, chehra ya nakhun neele ya pale [5][7]
- Saans tez, pasliyan dikhna, pet zyada hilna [7]
- Bolne mein dikkat ya saans lene mein badi mushkil [1][5]

q: mera 8 month ka baby bed se gir gaya aur ro raha hai
text:
Mere 8 mahine ke baby ke bed se girne ke baad, SEUP ke mutabiq yeh sir ka chot (traumatismo craneal) hai, jo aksar girne se hota hai [1]. Iske aam lakshan hain: sir dard, uljhan, thodi der ke liye yaad na rehna, chakkar, ji michalna, ulti aur neend aana [1].

Ghar par kya karein: SEUP ke mutabiq, agar sir dard ho to doctor ki bataayi hui khurak mein ibuprofen ya paracetamol de sakte hain [6]. Baby ko sone dein, lekin zyada bade chot mein har 4 ghante mein jagana chahiye [6]. Khaane mein koi khaas badlav zaroori nahi, apni bhookh ke hisaab se doodh ya khaana jaari rakhein [6]. Pehle 24 ghante tak nazar rakhein [3].

Turant madad lein agar:
- Tez ya badhta sir dard, ya dawa se bhi na sudhre [2]
- Baar baar ulti [2]
- Bechaini ya jagane par na uthna [2]
- Baat ya chalne mein dikkat, vyavhaar mein badlav [2]
- Naak ya kaan se khoon ya saaf paani [2]

SEUP ke mutabiq zyadatar bachche jaldi theek ho jaate hain [6].

q: 5 saal ke child ko body pe red rashes ho gaye hain
text:
5 saal ke bachche par red rashes ke kai kaaran ho sakte hain, aur inme se kuch aam aur bina ilaaj theek ho jaate hain. NHS ke mutabik, hives jaise rashes ke liye pharmacist se antihistamine ke baare mein salah li ja sakti hai, lekin chhote bachchon ke liye yeh treatment upyukt na ho [7]. WHO batati hai ki sarna (scabies) mein tez khujli hoti hai, khaas taur par raat mein, aur ungliyon, kalaiyon, baahon, pairon aur kamar ke aas-paas dane aur lines ban jaati hain; chhote bachchon mein yeh rash hatheli, talwe aur sar ki twacha par zyada gambhir ho sakta hai [2]. WHO ke mutabik sarna ka ilaaj cream ya dawa se hota hai [5].

Turant madad lein agar:
- Hoth, muh, gala ya jeebh achanak soojh jaaye [7]
- Saans tez ya mushkil ho, gala tight lage [7]
- Twacha, jeebh ya hoth neele, grey ya pale ho jaayein [7]
- Bachcha achanak confused, neend mein ya chakkar mein lage [7]
- Bachcha limp, floppy ya normal jaisa respond na kare [7]

q: kya polio ki drop dena zaroori hai
text:
Polio ki drop dena zaroori hai. WHO ke mutabiq, polio se bachav ke liye bachon ko polio vaccine (IPV) baaki routine vaccines ke saath di jaati hai, aur difteria ke saath mil kar lagne wali vaccine mein bhi polio vaccine shamil hoti hai [6].

Bharat ke national immunization schedule ke mutabiq, polio ki khaas drops (OPV) janm ke samay, 6, 10 aur 14 hafte par, aur phir 9 mahine par di jaati hain; IPV ki dose 6 hafte aur 14 hafte par lagti hai. Apne bachche ki umar ke hisaab se sahi dose ke liye apne doctor ya nazdeeki health centre se poochhein.

Agar aapke bachche ko bukhar hai, dast aa rahe hain, ya wo bimar lag raha hai, to vaccine dene se pehle doctor se salaah lein.
sources: [6] WHO — "Difteria", section "Prevención", p. 1 — https://www.who.int/es/news-room/fact-s

q: my baby has diarrhea after we came back from a trip
text:
Diarrhoea in a baby is usually an infection of the gut, and the main risk is dehydration, which is greater the smaller the child is [3]. Give oral rehydration salts (ORS) — a mixture of clean water, salt and sugar — in small amounts, and keep offering breast milk and nutrient-rich foods during the episode [1][3]. Zinc supplements shorten the episode by about 25% and reduce stool volume by about 30%, according to the WHO [1]. Do not use homemade solutions or fizzy drinks to replace lost fluids, and do not give medicines for diarrhoea or vomiting without asking your paediatrician [3].

Get help if:
- Much thirst, crying without tears, little urine, sunken eyes [3]
- Marked irritability, drowsiness or reduced responsiveness [3]
- Very watery, frequent stools and unable to drink fast enough [3]
- Refusing to eat or drink [3]
- Persistent or intense tummy pain, or stools with a lot of blood [3]

q: क्या टीका लगने के बाद बुखार आना सामान्य है?
text:
अगर बच्चा 3 महीने से छोटा है, तो बुखार होने पर उसी दिन डॉक्टर को दिखाना ज़रूरी है।

हाँ, टीके के बाद हल्का बुखार आना सामान्य है। डी.पी.टी. या डी.टी. का इंजेक्शन लगने के कुछ घंटों बाद बच्चे को हल्का बुखार हो सकता है, और ये दुष्प्रभाव सामान्य हैं — चिंता की बात नहीं [5]। खसरे के टीके के 6-7 दिनों बाद भी हल्का बुखार और शरीर पर हल्के लाल दाने हो सकते हैं; इनका इलाज ज़रूरी नहीं, ये अपने आप ठीक हो जाते हैं [5]।

डी.पी.टी. या डी.टी. के टीके के एक-दो घंटे बाद बच्चे को पेरासिटामॉल की गोली या शर्बत दी जा सकती है; खुराक के बारे में टीका लगाने वाले स्वास्थ्य कर्मचारी की सलाह मानें [5]। बच्चे की उम्र और वज़न के हिसाब से खुराक तय होती है।

डॉक्टर से मिलें अगर:
- बुखार या लक्षण 2-3 दिनों में ठीक न हों [5]
- इंजेक्शन की जगह लाल, गर्म या सूज जाए [5]

टीकों की उम्र और खुराक भारत के राष्ट्रीय टीकाकरण कार्यक्रम के अनुसार तय होती हैं।

बच्चे की उम्र कितनी है? उम्र जानकर मैं जवाब और सटीक कर सकता हूँ।

q: my child has been in the sun and now feels dizzy
text:
Heat illness happens when the body can't cool itself, usually after too long in the heat or sun, according to MedlinePlus [4]. Dizziness can be a sign of it [4].

What to do now: move your child to a cool, shaded place, take off extra clothing, put cool wet cloths on the forehead, neck and armpits, offer cool water in small sips, and use a fan to lower their temperature, according to the SEUP [6].

Get help if:
- Fever above 39°C that doesn't come down with home measures [7]
- Loss of consciousness or seizures [7]
- Confusion, trouble speaking or moving [7]
- Persistent vomiting and can't keep fluids down [7]
- Confusion, fainting, fast heartbeat or fast breathing [3]

If treated quickly, most children recover without complications, but without prompt treatment it can damage vital organs, according to the SEUP [6].

q: solids baby ko kab se dena shuru kare
text:
Solid khana shuru karne ka behtareen waqt takreeban 6 mahine ki umar hai, NHS ke mutabiq [2]. Is waqt tak maa ka doodh ya first infant formula hi bachay ki zyada tar energy aur nutrients faraham karta hai [4].

Shuru mein yeh zyada zaroori nahi ke bacha kitna khata hai — asal maqsad usay khane ki aadat dalna hai [2]. Doodh abhi bhi zyada tar ghiza deta rahega [2]. Aahista aahista miqdar aur qism barhate jayen, yahan tak ke bacha ghar ke khane ko chhote hisson mein kha sake [2].

Aap chahen to bacha khud apne haath se finger foods khaye, ya chammach se puree/mashed khana, ya dono ka mila jula tareeqa — koi ek tareeqa doosre se behtar nahi [1]. Kisi bhi tareeqe mein bacha apne haath se khaye to choking ka khatra chammach se khilane se zyada nahi hota [1].

Agar bacha waqt se pehle paida hua tha, to solid khana shuru karne ke waqt ke bare mein apne doctor se poochen [2].
